title: Scoped Privileged Roles: resource-driven RBAC v2 and migration plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement RBAC v2 focused on resource-scoped privileged roles for tenant, workspace and model-level operations. Deliverables include role/role-binding data model, permission matrix for built-in roles, API contract for evaluation, DB migration from RBAC v1, audit schema changes, SSO mapping guidance, and admin "break-glass" controls. Integrates with Console UX and policy enforcement in the policy-service.
acceptance_criteria: New role model deployed in policy-service behind feature flag and evaluated for 10% canary orgs
Permission matrix published in Confluence with examples and exportable CSV
Idempotent migration job created to map v1 assignments to v2 bindings with resumable checkpoints
Privileged actions emit structured audit events and surface in Console audit view
SSO/SAML sync flow documented with sample IdP configs and automated smoke tests
Canary rollback hooks and SLO-based automatic rollback implemented
design_decisions: Resource hierarchy chosen: organization > service_account > workspace > project > model > deployment > route
Two primitives: Role (set of typed permissions) and Binding (principal + role + resource scope). No role inheritance to keep evaluation O(1) per binding.
Permissions are verb.resource_type strings (e.g., deployments.start, models.publish) to allow simple membership checks and wildcard scoping.
Bindings stored as one row per principal+role+scope to make revocation and audit queries deterministic.
Break-glass implemented as time-limited EmergencyBinding entries with TTL, mandatory justification, and elevated audit tag.
tradeoffs: Avoiding inheritance reduces evaluation complexity but increases number of explicit roles for broad admin personas.
Flattened binding rows mean higher write amplification during large backfills but simplify real-time evaluation and deletes.
Wildcard scopes improve UX for admins but require stricter monitoring and alerting to catch over-broad grants.
Strongly-typed permissions increase onboarding lift for new features but reduce ambiguous grants and make audits reliable.
permission_matrix: OrgOwner => org.*, workspace.*, billing.*, users.manage, sso.configure
WorkspaceAdmin => workspace.*, project.*, model.*, deployments.manage, routes.manage
ScopedModelOps => model.publish, model.rollback, deployments.start (scoped to model:<id>)
api_contract_examples: POST /v1/rbac/bindings {principal_type:"user", principal_id:"u-123", role_id:"r-5", scope:"workspace:ws-234"} returns binding_id
migration_plan: Inventory: query RBAC v1 roles and ad-hoc grants per-org to build mapping table
Map: create authoritative mapping from v1 role names to v2 role definitions, flag ambiguous cases for manual review
Backfill: run batched job to insert Binding rows (5k org batch) with checkpoints and per-org rate limits
Dual-read: enable v2 evaluation behind feature flag while continuing to read v1 for fallback during cutover
Retention: keep v1 records immutable for 30 days post-cutover to support rollback and audits
audit_logging_requirements: All privileged/admin actions emit structured events with: timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, scope, outcome, request_id, payload_hash
Audit events are append-only and written to the audit-store with retention: 365 days for enterprise, 90 days standard
Console must provide filtering by actor, action, resource, time range and link to trace/session when available
Break-glass usage must generate high-severity alerts including justification and linked incident ticket
sso_saml_notes: Support mapping SAML groups/attributes to role bindings using declarative sync rules (e.g., saml:groups contains 'infra-admin' => bind OrgOwner with TTL)
Offer Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning for transient bindings; JIT grants require explicit TTL and audit entry
Provide admin UI to preview effective bindings from a sample SAML assertion before applying mapping rules
Publish sample IdP config snippets for Okta and Azure AD and include SAML attribute names used for mapping
rollout_plan: Phase 0: implement schema and feature-flagged endpoints; internal QA against synthetic orgs (2 weeks)
Phase 1: canary with 10% of non-critical orgs and early enterprise partners; monitor auth errors, latency, and audit volume
Phase 2: enable Console role-binding UX and break-glass workflows; update onboarding and security docs
Phase 3: full migration job run with parallel-read of RBAC v1 for 30 days; finalize cutover and retire v1 after validation
